reasons: Only the first three of thirteen sections were visible, so most of the file could not be checked.
A test file exists for the navigation helper, which is good evidence for that part.
I did not run the code.

terms.meaning: The outer frame of the app that stays the same while the page content changes.
A short name for each menu item, used to match links to labels.
The main workflow links, such as documents and verification.
Supporting links such as family, parcel and timeline.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and default case
sections.what: Brings in the link and path tools, the language and translation helpers, the village background, and React. Sets the demo case ID used when no other is given.
sections.why: Gives the shell what it needs and provides a default demo case.
sections.watch_out: The default case ID is a demo value, so a real deployment must not rely on it.

sections.name: CaseNavigationKey
sections.title: Navigation key names
sections.what: Lists the eleven names used for case navigation links, such as dashboard, documents, verification, parcel, earth and timeline.
sections.why: Gives each menu item a fixed name so the labels and links can be matched reliably.
sections.watch_out: A new menu item needs a new name here, or the label lookup will not work.

sections.name: CaseNavigationLink
sections.title: Navigation link builder
sections.what: For a given case ID, returns two lists of links. The primary list holds the core workflow pages. The context list holds supporting pages such as family, parcel, official records, earth observation and timeline.
sections.why: Builds all case links from one place so every link uses the same case ID.
sections.watch_out: Each link path is built from the case ID, so a wrong ID sends the user to the wrong case.

sections.name: RailNavigation (part 1)
sections.title: Left icon rail, part one
sections.what: Starts the vertical icon menu on the left side of the screen. It has a logo that returns home, links to the home page and to this case's dashboard, and links to the Differences and Evidence sections of the case. The link for the current page is highlighted.
sections.why: Likely reason: a compact menu that stays visible while moving between case sections. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Links are built from defaultCaseId, so changing the default case changes every rail link, and the highlight depends on matching the path text.

sections.name: RailNavigation (part 2)
sections.title: Left icon rail, part two
sections.what: Finishes the rail with the Documents link and a language button. The button shows the other language name and switches the whole site between English and Hindi, and it is hidden on small screens.
sections.why: Likely reason: the language switch sits at the bottom of the rail and is hidden on phones where space is tight. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The button label shows the other language, so a wrong label would confuse users, and the hide class must stay on the button for the small-screen layout to work.

sections.name: TopBar
sections.title: Top bar with back button and language switch
sections.what: Builds the top bar on each page: the logo, a Back button on every page except the home page, a short notice, a language switch, and a call to action that opens the user's case. The text comes from the Hindi or English copy for the current language.
sections.why: Likely reason: a consistent header that gives a way back and a clear next step on every page. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The Back button is hidden only when the path is exactly the home page, so any new route with a different home path would still show it.

sections.name: SiteHeader
sections.title: Empty site header placeholder
sections.what: Exists as a named component that renders nothing. Users see no change from it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Anything expecting a header here will get nothing, so do not add content here expecting it to appear.

sections.name: CaseNavigationLinks
sections.title: Row of case navigation chips
sections.what: Draws a row of small link buttons for a list of case pages. The link matching the current page is highlighted in lime and marked as the current page for screen readers.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared row builder keeps the two link groups looking the same. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Highlighting uses an exact text match on the link address, so a trailing slash or a hash part would stop the highlight from showing.

sections.name: CaseNavigation
sections.title: Case sub-navigation bar
sections.what: Shows the sub-menu for one case as a wrapping row with a primary group of links and a context group of links. The bar sits above case content.
sections.why: Likely reason: case pages need a second level of navigation separate from the left rail. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The link lists come from caseNavigationSections, which is not shown here, and the labels come from translation keys, so a missing key would show a blank chip.

sections.name: Notice
sections.title: Empty notice placeholder
sections.what: Exists as a named component that renders nothing. Users see no change from it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The visible notice text comes from the top bar and page code instead, so this placeholder should not be relied on.

sections.name: SiteFooter
sections.title: Site footer
sections.what: Shows the footer line at the bottom of each page in the chosen language. The text says the site is an independent prototype and uses no real government records.
sections.why: Likely reason: a permanent reminder of the prototype's status on every page. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The footer text is read from the shared copy file, so a change there changes every page at once.

sections.name: CaseHeader
sections.title: Case page heading
sections.what: Shows the large case title and a smaller subtitle at the top of a case page.
sections.why: Likely reason: case pages share one heading style. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Title and subtitle are passed in by each page, so an empty value leaves a blank heading.

sections.name: AppShell
sections.title: Overall page layout
sections.what: Puts the page together: the animated village background behind everything, the left rail, the top bar, a short notice, the page content, and the footer. Each page's content is passed in and appears in the main area.
sections.why: Likely reason: one wrapper gives every page the same frame. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The village background is a separate animated layer, so heavy changes to it could slow every page.

summary: The layout frame for the app, which sets up the navigation menus, the case header and the top and bottom bars. Only part of the file was visible to me, so this description is partial.
purpose: Gives every page a consistent frame with navigation to the core case workflow and to context pages.
why: Likely reason: one shared frame keeps the navigation the same on every screen. Reason partly stated in the outline and the navigation helper.
how: Defines the navigation keys, then a helper that builds the primary and context links for a given case ID. The rest of the file, which I could not see in full, builds the rail, the top bar, the links, the notice, the footer, the case header and the overall app shell.
inputs: A case ID, the current web address, and the current language.
outputs: Navigation links and the layout around every page.
risks: Only the first three sections were visible. Changing the navigation helper changes the links on every case page.
debug: If a menu item is missing or links to the wrong case, check the navigation helper and the case ID. If the frame is missing, check the app shell in the unseen part of the file.
